$comment: Version-keyed Rust stabilizations, gated on the crate's MSRV before they reach an agent.
Why this is data and not prose: a model's training data lags the toolchain, and even when
it knows the new API it writes the old shape out of habit. Naming the new API in a rule
fixes the first half and makes the second half worse — an agent told about `bool::ok_or`
on a crate whose `rust-version` is 1.70 writes code that does not compile. So the list
lives here, `hooks/scripts/stdlib-timeline.ts` filters it to the crate's floor, and
`inject-rules.ts` emits only what that crate can actually use.
Maintaining it: add an entry per release for stabilizations that REPLACE a shape a model
still reaches for by default. Not a changelog — an entry earns its place by displacing a
habit. `instead` is the habit; keep it concrete enough to recognize in a diff.
`clippy` names the lint that mechanizes the swap (verify with `clippy-driver -Whelp`,
which prints hyphenated names) or is omitted when no lint exists.
`kind` is "idiom" (reach for this) or "breakage" (expect this, do not work around it).

entries.instead: the `match` / `if let` ladder that exists only to `return` on the miss
`lazy_static!` or `once_cell::sync::OnceCell` for one-shot init
`map_or(false, …)`
the `(a + b - 1) / b` rounding trick
`#[async_trait]` — which still earns its place when the trait must be `dyn`-safe
`map_err(|e| { log(&e); e })` — a side effect wearing a transform's clothes
`CString::new("…").unwrap()` — a runtime panic path for a compile-time constant
`once_cell::sync::Lazy`
take, inspect, then put the value back on the reject path
bare `#[allow]` — `expect` fires when the suppression stops being needed, so it cannot rot silently
`map_or(true, …)`
the nested `if let` pyramid
the match-arm-then-nested-`if let` shape — `Foo(a) if let Some(b) = lookup(a) => …`
push, then `last_mut().unwrap()` to get the reference back
`assert!(matches!(…))`, which prints no value when it fails (see testing.md)
hand-rolled `leading_zeros` arithmetic
the `if !cond { return Err(…) }` guard — `cond.ok_or(Error::Invalid)?`
pointer arithmetic to recover a sub-slice's offset
the `strip_prefix` + `strip_suffix` pair
parse-then-check
copying plain data to borrow it as atomics

entries.item: some `ambiguous_glob_imports` are hard errors, `T = T` where-bounds are rejected, and `invalid_runtime_symbol_definitions` is denied
entries.instead: A build that was warning-clean on 1.97 can go red on these alone; that is a toolchain fact to report, not code to work around.
